title: What you will be able to do
instruction: Press reveal to see each outcome for this lesson.

_items.text: Use discipline-specific vocabulary precisely, signalling fluency in your field's own discourse.

title: Vocabulary that marks who you are writing for
body: Every discipline has words that carry a specific, settled meaning inside it, a meaning a general reader would not necessarily guess. Using these words precisely signals that you are writing inside the discipline, not about it from outside.

title: What counts as discipline-specific vocabulary
body: Dennis and Abbott (2026, pp.131-133) frame the question directly: 'What constitutes discipline-specific vocabulary? Included here are individual words or terms that carry meaning within the disciplinary discourse.' The book follows this with a task extract for you to analyse in the same way, if you have the text to hand.

title: Worked example
body:
Consider two drafts written for the same discipline-specific audience.

{{learner-a}} avoids a field's own terms entirely, explaining everything in general language, which reads as unfamiliar with the discipline.

{{learner-b}} uses the field's own terms precisely and in the right place, signalling fluency without having to announce it.

Both drafts were accurate. Only {{learner-b}}'s draft read as written by someone inside the field.

title: Why precision matters more than volume
body: Using a discipline's vocabulary does not mean using more jargon. It means using the right term, correctly, exactly where the field itself would use it, and no term where the field would not.

definition: Individual words or terms that carry meaning within a disciplinary discourse (Dennis and Abbott, 2026, p.131).
extendedDefinition: A term can be ordinary outside a field and carry a precise, technical meaning inside it; using it correctly signals membership in that field's discourse.
example: A term used loosely by a general reader but precisely by a specialist is an example of discipline-specific vocabulary.

displayTitle: A passage, marked for discipline-specific terms
instruction: Select a highlighted term to see why it counts as discipline-specific.

_passage._note: A precise, technical term inside this field; a general reader might read 'validity' alone and miss the specific claim being made.
A term that names a specific method choice, not just 'the way the study was done'.

title: Building your own vocabulary
body: Keep a short list of your own discipline's terms as you meet them, each with the precise meaning it carries inside your field. Try the book's own task extract on pages 132-133 if you have it to hand, checking your reading against it.

title: Your turn
instruction: This is for your own reflection; no right answers are expected.

_items.text: Name one term from your own discipline that means something different, or more precise, than it does in general use.
Is there a term you have been using loosely that your discipline actually defines precisely?
